newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Lindsey says U.S. economy "quite good".
newsitem.headline: Fed's Lindsey says U.S. economy "quite good".

text.p: Outgoing Federal Reserve Board Governor Lawrence Lindsey said the U.S. economy appears to be in good shape.
"I think it's quite good," Lindsey said in a CNBC interview. "We continue to have strong growth (and) relatively low inflation."

Lindsey said he prefered to analyze nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) when mulling Fed policy. Money supply statistics used to influence policymakers before they lost much of their correlation with GDP, he said.
"We have to wait for more data before we become as convinced as we were in the early '90s that M2 is a good indicator of where the economy is going," Lindsey said.
The outgoing Fed governor said the U.S. must rein in entitlement spending.
"Long term, we have to get control of our entitlement situation. Ideally, we have to do so without raising taxes," he said.
